About Lucid

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid's proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our "Compromise Nothing™" approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.

We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what's possible and shape the future of mobility.

  

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced and forward-thinking Staff CAD / PLM Engineer (Tools & Methods) to lead the architecture, standardization, and evolution of our enterprise CAD and Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) ecosystem.

In this role, you will be the technical authority defining how vehicle engineering data is created, governed, and integrated across enterprise systems. You will lead the transition to next-generation platforms (Dassault Systèmes 3DEXPERIENCE), drive seamless data interfaces with SAP ERP (iPPE), author enterprise-level MCAD exchange standards, and build robust MBSE/Requirements traceability workflows from initial systems architecture down to production manufacturing deliverables.

Key Responsibilities

1. 3DEXPERIENCE Platform Architecture & Evolution • Lead technical workstreams for major enterprise platform upgrades (e.g., 3DEXPERIENCE 2026x), defining validation scenarios, managing lower environments, and resolving blocked actions. • Architect and maintain default enterprise workspace structures, ENOVIA dashboard frameworks, and SWYM community access models. • Partner with enterprise IT and PLM development teams to define and refine the 3DX – SAP BOM interface (Phase 2 / iPPE), establishing single-source-of-truth data governance for engineering release timelines and revision controls.

2. CAD Methods, Tooling & Start Part Standardization • Own and standardize enterprise-wide CAD Start Parts (Sheet Metal, Plastic A-side WIP, Castings/Machining WIP), integrating standard datum schemes, Power Copies, part markings, and manufacturing info styling (GCPs, parting lines). • Develop advanced modeling methodologies for complex disciplines, including electrical wire harness integration (deformable/flattened models, suffix configurations) and captive fasteners (Parts-In-Assembly / PIA) with torque attributes. • Define and automate Digital Mock-Up (DMU) clash analysis and space-claim verification using configuration-driven vehicle packaging tools.

3. MCAD Data Exchange & Supplier Governance • Author, maintain, and enforce enterprise MCAD Data Exchange Standards governing 3D model and 2D drawing exchange between Lucid and Tier-1/Tier-2 suppliers. • Establish Product Data Quality (PDQ) thresholds, geometry quality check profiles (e.g., LCQC/Q-Checker), naming conventions, and formal unit exception workflows.

4. Requirements Management & MBSE Traceability • Drive Functional Specification Documents (FSDs) and UAT execution for linking 3DX Requirements (TRM) to Technical Product Documentation (TPD). • Operationalize Requirements, Functional, Logical, and Physical (RFLP) workflows and one-way synchronizations between Model-Based Systems Engineering tools (Cameo / No Magic) and 3DX.

5. Technical Leadership, Community Enablement & Tier-3 Support • Lead the monthly 3DX Champions / Super-User Forums, presenting on tool deployments, automated drawing rollouts (LADS), and emerging AI-assisted CAD tools. • Serve as the senior escalation point (Tier-3) for complex CAD modeling bottlenecks, geometry issues, and PLM workflow blockers. • Manage and prioritize feature requests, bugs, and development backlogs in Jira (Epics, user stories, and acceptance criteria).

Qualifications & Experience

Required:

* Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Automotive Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience.

* Experience: 8+ years of dedicated experience in CAD/PLM systems engineering, tools & methods, or CAD quality administration within the Automotive, Aerospace, or High-Tech Manufacturing industries.

* Dassault Systèmes Expertise: Deep technical proficiency in 3DEXPERIENCE (CATIA V6, ENOVIA, TRM/RFLP, DMU), including native client administration, Power Copies, and template development.

* Enterprise Integration: Direct experience with PLM-to-ERP integrations, particularly SAP iPPE (Integrated Product and Process Engineering) and engineering bill of materials (eBOM / mBOM) lifecycles.

* Standards Authoring: Proven track record authoring enterprise engineering specifications, ASME Y14.5 / ISO geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) guidelines, and MCAD supplier data protocols.

* Requirements & MBSE: Working knowledge of MBSE methodologies, Cameo/SysML modeling, and traceability to physical engineering releases.

**Cal Poly Pomona Enterprises Employment Services**

  

**ANNOUNCEMENT OF POSITION VACANCY**

  

**SUMMARY**: Graduate Research Assistant - Food Bioprocessing and Smart Manufacturing The Department of Nutrition and Food Science is seeking two motivated graduate students to join a collaborative research program led by Dr. Mohammad Zarei. The positions are supported through the NSF Center for Research Advancement in Smart Manufacturing (CREST-RASM) and connect hands-on food-science experimentation with process monitoring, data analysis, modeling, and digital-twin validation. Students will work with food science and engineering collaborators and contribute to publishable research in sustainable food manufacturing. Current projects include the valorization of tomato seed meal, sorghum distillers dried grains with solubles (DDGS), and California alfalfa through enzymatic hydrolysis and fermentation. These are representative projects rather than the limits of the appointment. Depending on project needs and student interests, assignments may also involve alternative and plant proteins, agricultural and food by-product biorefineries, extrusion processing, bioactive peptides, sustainable packaging and bioplastics, functional foods, downstream processing, cultivated-food applications, and AI-assisted process optimization

* Food bioprocessing and biorefinery systems: protein extraction, concentration, enzymatic hydrolysis, fermentation, separation, and recovery.

* Alternative proteins and value-added ingredients: plant proteins, protein hydrolysates, bioactive peptides, functional ingredients, and applications in food or feed.

* Smart food manufacturing: real-time monitoring, sensor data, experimental design, process optimization, and validation of data-driven or digital-twin models.

* Food process engineering and sustainable materials: extrusion, ingredient functionality, texture and rheology, bioplastics, and sustainable packaging when relevant to active projects.

* Plan and conduct laboratory experiments under approved protocols, including preparation of raw materials, reagents, enzymes, cultures, and samples.

* Operate and help maintain research equipment such as stirred-tank bioreactors, the Labfors 5 and Eppendorf SciVario Twin platforms, twin-screw extrusion systems, texture and viscosity instruments, and other analytical tools after training.

* Monitor process variables; collect, organize, and quality-check experimental data; and maintain complete electronic and laboratory records.

* Analyze results using appropriate statistical and visualization tools and prepare figures, tables, presentations, posters, reports, and manuscript materials.

* Work with engineering collaborators to provide experimental datasets and compare laboratory results with simulations, predictive models, and digital twins.

* Follow laboratory safety, biosafety, sanitation, quality-assurance, and waste-management procedures; help organize supplies and shared laboratory spaces.

* Participate in regular research meetings, communicate progress, troubleshoot experiments, and support undergraduate researchers when appropriate.

* Currently enrolled in a Cal Poly Pomona graduate program in food science, nutrition and food science, food engineering, biotechnology, biological sciences, chemical engineering, or a closely related field, and in good academic standing.

* Relevant coursework or laboratory experience in food chemistry, food microbiology, food engineering, biochemistry, biotechnology, or bioprocessing.

* Ability to work safely and carefully in a laboratory, follow protocols, maintain accurate records, and manage multiple research tasks.

* Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work independently and collaboratively with an interdisciplinary team.

* Availability to work approximately 10 hours per week, including scheduled laboratory blocks required for experiments.

  

**PREFFERED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Experience with protein extraction, enzymatic hydrolysis, microbial fermentation, bioreactors, extrusion, membrane separation, or food-product analysis.

* Familiarity with experimental design, statistics, data visualization, or software such as Excel, JMP, R, Python, MATLAB, or comparable tools.

* Interest in sustainable food processing, smart manufacturing, sensors, automation, artificial intelligence, or digital-twin applications.

* Interest in presenting research, co-authoring publications, mentoring undergraduate students, and pursuing research intensive careers or doctoral study.

Melissa is looking for a curious, detail-oriented, and technically capable data professional to help maintain and improve the quality of some of our most important proprietary data assets. At Melissa, we develop data quality and identity solutions that help organizations maintain accurate, reliable, and connected information.

We are looking for someone to take a hands-on role in understanding, analyzing, validating, and continuously improving these identifiers. You will work directly with large datasets, investigate data anomalies, develop quality checks, evaluate changes, and collaborate with technical teams to ensure our identifiers remain accurate, consistent, and reliable. * Develop repeatable data-quality checks, reports, and automated validation processes.

* Collaborate with Data Production, Programming, and Quality Assurance teams to investigate and resolve issues.

jobs.description:
**About Onos Health**

Onos Health’s mission is simple but ambitious: ensure every healthcare dollar goes toward delivering the highest quality care. Today, nearly 30% of U.S. healthcare spending is wasted due to ineffective care and administrative burden caused by misalignment between providers and payers.

Onos is addressing this by building the AI platform that enables health plans to understand clinical care at scale. By transforming unstructured clinical documentation into actionable insights, we help payers make faster, more informed decisions, identify opportunities to improve quality and reduce waste, and ensure more healthcare dollars are directed toward delivering better outcomes.

Come join a category-defining company and transform how healthcare is managed in the U.S.

**Why Onos?**

Meaningful impact: Help solve one of healthcare’s biggest challenges by improving quality while reducing waste.

Ownership: Take on significant responsibility from day one and shape a rapidly growing company.

Direct collaboration: Work alongside experienced founders with deep expertise in healthcare, AI, and product development.

High-performing team: Join a transparent, collaborative, and execution-focused culture.

Build something new: Help define the next generation of AI-powered healthcare analytics.

**The Role**

We’re looking for a Senior Data Analyst to turn health plan data into the reporting, analyses, and insights our customers rely on.

You’ll work hands-on with claims, authorization, eligibility, and clinical review data from our health plan customers. You’ll build and maintain the analyses and dashboards that show customers what’s happening in their populations: utilization trends, provider variation, cost, and the impact of programs running on the Onos platform.

This role works closely with our data science, product, and customer teams. This role is tightly focused on core analytics – tackling complex analytical questions independently. You’ll own analyses end to end, from digging into data to presenting results to customer stakeholders, and you’ll help make repeatable analyses into standard reporting in the product.

**What You’ll Be Doing**

**Customer Analytics & Reporting**

* Build and maintain customer-facing reports and dashboards covering utilization, cost, provider performance, and program outcomes.
* Run analyses that answer specific customer questions, such as where spend is concentrated, which providers are outliers, and how a program is affecting utilization.
* Support ROI and impact analyses by preparing data, running calculations, and checking results against agreed methodologies.
* Prepare findings for customer meetings and present results to analytics and operational teams at health plans.

**Data Onboarding & Quality**

* Explore and analyze structured, analysis-ready customer data feeds (including claims, authorizations, eligibility, and clinical documentation) to extract key insights.
* Investigate data quality issues, anomalies, and inconsistencies, collaborating closely with Engineering and customer teams to ensure accurate reporting.
* Partner with Data Engineering to define business logic and data requirements needed for downstream analytical workflows.
* Build checks that catch data issues before they reach customer reporting.

**Product Support**

* Turn recurring customer analyses into standard metrics and reports that can be built into the platform.
* Help define metric logic and business rules so numbers are consistent across customers and reports.
* Give Product, Engineering, and Data Science feedback on what customers ask for and where current reporting falls short.

**Collaborate Across the Company**

* Work with Data Science, Product, Engineering, Clinical Operations, and Customer Success on customer engagements and internal projects.
* Be a go-to resource on how our customers’ data is structured and what it can and can’t support.

**What We’re Looking For**

* 4+ years of experience in healthcare analytics or a related analytical role.
* Hands-on experience with healthcare claims data; experience with authorization, eligibility, or clinical data is a plus.
* Strong SQL skills, working proficiency in Python for data analysis, and proven ability to independently answer complex, ambiguous analytical questions.
* Experience building dashboards and reports in a BI or notebook tool.
* Solid understanding of descriptive statistics and common healthcare metrics (e.g., PMPM, utilization per 1,000, cost per member).
* Careful about data quality, with a habit of checking results before sharing them.
* Ability to explain analytical findings clearly to non-technical audiences.
* Proven experience working directly with customers or external stakeholders is required.
* Comfortable working in ambiguity and building processes from the ground up.
* Healthcare payer, provider, or health technology experience strongly preferred. Behavioral health experience is a plus.
* Exceptional references from colleagues and former managers.

**Why This Role Is Unique**

At Onos, Analysts aren’t a back-office reporting function.

You’ll work directly with health plan customers, see how your analyses inform their decisions, and help shape the reporting built into the Onos platform.

If you like digging into messy healthcare data, getting the numbers right, and seeing your work used by customers, we’d love to talk.

jobs.title: Research Associate II, R&D
jobs.description:
**About Mission Bio**

Based in South San Francisco, Mission Bio is the leader in single cell, multi-omics solutions for precision medicine. Our mission is to empower researchers and clinicians to eradicate cancer, and our Tapestri® Platform is at the center of that effort. As the industry’s first high throughput single cell, multi-omics solution, Tapestri is trusted by leading academic medical centers, cancer institutes, and biopharma companies to advance research and accelerate the development of curative therapies, including the future of cell and gene therapy.

We are entering an exciting growth phase focused on innovation, deeper commercial partnerships, and broader clinical adoption. Our expanded tri-omics capabilities now combine targeted gene expression and genotyping in a single assay, opening up new opportunities across oncology and therapeutic development.

**Position Overview**

We are looking for a highly motivated individual to join the Research and Development (R&D) team as a Research Associate II. The successful candidate will play a key role in driving successful completion of novel custom multi-omics single-cell projects in coordination with Bioinformatics and R&D teams. The position will be critical in generating analytical and experimental data for Mission Bio’s customers across diverse applications in cell and gene therapy, drug, and biomarker development.

  

This position will report to the R&D Team Lead.

**Core Responsibilities:**

* Prepare, handle, and/or culture human cell lines and primary cells for testing on Mission Bio’s single-cell Tapestri platform.
* Execute experiments following complex plans and protocols on the Tapestri platform, including downstream NGS library preparation and sequencing.
* Operate a variety of lab instruments, including automated cell counter, microscope, Bioanalyzer, etc., to evaluate sample quality.
* Perform routine maintenance of laboratory equipment and upkeep of electronic databases.
* Plan and coordinate with team members to troubleshoot protocols and optimize workflows.
* Prepare written protocols for new processes and/or update existing protocols.
* Present experimental results and project updates in written and verbal formats to manager and other members of a multidisciplinary team.
* Maintain project deadlines while working on a variety of projects at one time.
* Perform occasional cross-functional collaborative experiments based on company priorities.

  

**Essential Skills, Education, and Experience:**

* A Bachelor’s (B.S./B.A.) or Master’s (MS) degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Biochemistry or related field.
* At least 2 years of hands-on lab experience. Industry experience is preferred.
* Experience with analytical, molecular, and/or cellular biology techniques. Some examples include, PCR, real-time PCR, NGS library prep, fluorescence microscopy, and/or cell culture techniques. Single-cell and NGS experience is strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated strong technical laboratory, analytical and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to adapt in a fast-paced environment while maintaining a high level of data quality.
* Self-starter with excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
* Excellent communication skills with demonstrated success working effectively in cross-functional teams.
* Ability to uphold Mission Bio’s core values (impact, entrepreneurship, teamwork).

  

**Physical Demands & Work Environment**

* **Physical Demands:**

### **Company Description**

**Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!**

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.

### **Job Description**

The Center for Global Security Research (CGSR) was established at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in 1996 to bring together experts from the science, technology, and policy communities to address pressing national security challenges. For over 20 years, CGSR has engaged diverse perspectives on topics important to national security, deterrence, diplomacy, dual-use technology, arms control, nonproliferation, space, cyber, biosecurity, and energy security.

We have openings in Summer 2027 for undergraduate students to engage in practical research on global security topics. Students will work with CGSR over the duration of three to four months as a research associate (RA). RAs will engage in practical research to further their educational and career goals, while also supporting the development of strategies for national security and LLNL’s mission focus areas. Examples of relevant fields of research include nuclear deterrence, arms control, nonproliferation, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, space, biological & chemical security, and energy security.

*This position offers a hybrid schedule, blending in-person and virtual presence. You will have the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week.*

CGSR’s objectives are as follows:

* To explore the dynamics of potential 21st century strategic conflicts (i.e., those with a potential nuclear aspect) and to formulate ideas about how to achieve U.S. deterrence and other objectives in such conflicts.
* To explore the sources and characteristics of strategic competition in the emerging security environment and to formulate organizing concepts to enhance the competitive position of the United States and its allies and partners over the long term.
* To identify whether and how technically based approaches can address new challenges to national and international security.
* To catalyze broader national and international thinking about the requirements of effective deterrence, assurance, and strategic stability in a changed and changing security environment.
* To assist in the development of new generations of experts motivated by a clear view of the changed and changing security environment.

More information on CGSR, its research focus areas, and its publications can be found at https://cgsr.llnl.gov/.

This job will be closed to applicants on February 1, 2027.

**You will**

* Conduct an independent research project on an agreed upon topic aligned with CGSR/LLNL research priorities under the supervision of CGSR staff.
* Support CGSR/LLNL through contributions to ongoing research activities. Tasks may include contributing to literature reviews, annotated bibliographies, and workshop summary reports.
* Attend relevant research seminars, speakers’ series, and workshops.
* Present research to LLNL staff at end of the assignment.
* Prepare end-of-assignment technical report or publication.
* Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

### **Qualifications**

* Must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). See Additional Information section below for details.
* Must be currently enrolled in an accredited university or have completed AA/AS degree in a field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Areas of study include international relations and/or security, political science, economics, public policy, emerging technologies, nonproliferation, energy, biosecurity, foreign language studies, or related fields.
* Demonstrated academic and/or professional achievement in a relevant field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities.
* Strong record of independent research and publication, or a strong proposal of research to be done while at CGSR and in future academic and professional settings.
* Ability to work in a team environment.

$23.26 - $31.62 Hourly
  
  
This position is under a step structure. Please note that the step placement is determined by your most recent completed academic year.

### **Additional Information**

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

* Included in 2026 Best Places to Work by Glassdoor!

* Sick leave accrual

None required. However, if your assignment is longer than 179 days cumulatively within a calendar year, you must go through the Personal Identity Verification process. This process includes completing an online background investigation form and receiving approval of the background check.

### **About DeepOrigin**

Deep Origin is building ambitious science in a fast-moving environment, combining AI and physics-based methods with wet-lab biology to advance drug discovery. The people who thrive here are accountable, adaptable, rigorous, humble, and direct. Across roles, we look for:

* **Ownership through to the result.** An experiment isn't done until the data are analyzed, the conclusion is written down, and whoever needs it next has it.
* **Judgment under incomplete information.** You resolve what you need to know, commit to a defensible course of action, and revise when the evidence warrants it.
* **Exacting about the work, unguarded about yourself.** You hold data to a standard that survives scrutiny, and you drop your own interpretation when someone shows you better evidence.
* **Transparency as a working habit.** You surface problems while they are cheap to fix, and you explain your results so chemists, engineers, and computational colleagues can act on them.

### **About the role**

We are hiring a hands-on **Senior Research Associate** to build and run the cell-based assays and engineered cell lines behind our drug discovery programs. You will work day to day with a senior scientist in R&D, owning bench execution while helping shape assay strategy.

Your core work: maintaining mammalian cell lines, engineering them with RNP-based CRISPR (knockouts and knock-ins), generating validated stable lines, and turning them into robust functional assays. The data you generate feeds directly into AI and physics-based compound design, so quality and reproducibility matter as much as throughput.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

 **Requirements**  

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in biology, cell biology, bioengineering, biochemistry, immunology, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Relevant hands-on laboratory experience
* Demonstrated mammalian cell culture experience with strong aseptic technique, including routine maintenance of multiple lines in parallel.
* Hands-on experience with CRISPR gene editing: knockout generation, and ideally knock-in, with validation of edited clones.
* Experience with transient transfection, and with generating and validating stable cell lines, including clonal selection and banking.
* Experience executing at least one cell-based assay readout, such as flow cytometry, plate-based viability, reporter, or proliferation assays.
* Ability to analyze data, assess assay quality, communicate findings clearly, and work in a collaborative, multidisciplinary setting.
* Commitment to laboratory safety, research integrity, accurate documentation, and responsible handling of biological materials.

### **Nice to have qualifications**

* Hands-on RNP-based CRISPR knockout and knock-in using Lonza Nucleofector platforms (4D-Nucleofector or equivalent), including program and buffer selection for the target cell type.
* Experience with high-throughput or automated assay platforms, including 96- or 384-channel electronic pipetting systems and benchtop pipetting robots (INTEGRA VIAFLO, MINI 96, VOYAGER, ASSIST PLUS or comparable), and multimode plate readers.
* Experience developing or optimizing BRET, TR-FRET/HTRF, or related proximity-based assay formats .
* Molecular biology bench skills: construct and primer design, cloning, qPCR or digital PCR, Western blot.
* Drug discovery experience in biotech or pharma, including work on a target-to-lead or lead-optimization program.
* Familiarity with assay qualification concepts: design of experiments, dose-response analysis, curve fitting, acceptance criteria, and statistical assessment of assay variability.
* Experience with neuronal or other CNS-relevant cell models. .
* Experience with multiplexed editing, including triple knockouts or combined knockout and knock-in lines.

### **Key responsibilities**

**Mammalian cell culture**

* Culture, expand, and maintain mammalian cell lines under strict aseptic technique; monitor health, viability, density, and passage history.
* Maintain cryopreserved stocks, run mycoplasma and identity checks, and keep accurate lineage records.

**Genome engineering**

* Optimize RNP-based CRISPR/Cas editing in mammalian cell lines: single and double knockouts.
* Design and execute targeted knock-in strategies, including donor design, delivery optimization, and editing-efficiency assessment.

**Stable cell line generation**

* Perform transient transfections to test constructs quickly, optimizing reagent, nucleic acid amount, and harvest timing, and confirming expression before committing to a stable line.
* Generate stable lines using viral and non-viral delivery; perform clonal selection, expansion, functional validation, and banking.
* Characterize clones for expression level, assay performance, and stability over passage.

**Cell-based assay development**

* Develop, optimize, and run functional assays: plate-based, reporter and proximity-based assays; flow cytometry; and other cellular functional readouts.
* Optimize seeding density, stimulation conditions, dose range, incubation time, controls, and acceptance criteria to improve sensitivity, dynamic range, and reproducibility.

**Data, documentation, and communication**

* Analyze dose-response data, fit curves, assess assay quality (Z', signal window, variability), and flag trends, outliers, and deviations.

new_jobs.description:
### **Company Description**

**Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!**

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.

### **Job Description**

The Center for Global Security Research (CGSR) was established at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in 1996 to bring together experts from the science, technology, and policy communities to address pressing national security challenges. For over 20 years, CGSR has engaged diverse perspectives on topics important to national security, deterrence, diplomacy, dual-use technology, arms control, nonproliferation, space, cyber, biosecurity, and energy security.

We have openings in Summer 2027 for undergraduate students to engage in practical research on global security topics. Students will work with CGSR over the duration of three to four months as a research associate (RA). RAs will engage in practical research to further their educational and career goals, while also supporting the development of strategies for national security and LLNL’s mission focus areas. Examples of relevant fields of research include nuclear deterrence, arms control, nonproliferation, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, space, biological & chemical security, and energy security.

*This position offers a hybrid schedule, blending in-person and virtual presence. You will have the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week.*

CGSR’s objectives are as follows:

* To explore the dynamics of potential 21st century strategic conflicts (i.e., those with a potential nuclear aspect) and to formulate ideas about how to achieve U.S. deterrence and other objectives in such conflicts.
* To explore the sources and characteristics of strategic competition in the emerging security environment and to formulate organizing concepts to enhance the competitive position of the United States and its allies and partners over the long term.
* To identify whether and how technically based approaches can address new challenges to national and international security.
* To catalyze broader national and international thinking about the requirements of effective deterrence, assurance, and strategic stability in a changed and changing security environment.
* To assist in the development of new generations of experts motivated by a clear view of the changed and changing security environment.

More information on CGSR, its research focus areas, and its publications can be found at https://cgsr.llnl.gov/.

This job will be closed to applicants on February 1, 2027.

**You will**

* Conduct an independent research project on an agreed upon topic aligned with CGSR/LLNL research priorities under the supervision of CGSR staff.
* Support CGSR/LLNL through contributions to ongoing research activities. Tasks may include contributing to literature reviews, annotated bibliographies, and workshop summary reports.
* Attend relevant research seminars, speakers’ series, and workshops.
* Present research to LLNL staff at end of the assignment.
* Prepare end-of-assignment technical report or publication.
* Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

### **Qualifications**

* Must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). See Additional Information section below for details.
* Must be currently enrolled in an accredited university or have completed AA/AS degree in a field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Areas of study include international relations and/or security, political science, economics, public policy, emerging technologies, nonproliferation, energy, biosecurity, foreign language studies, or related fields.
* Demonstrated academic and/or professional achievement in a relevant field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities.
* Strong record of independent research and publication, or a strong proposal of research to be done while at CGSR and in future academic and professional settings.
* Ability to work in a team environment.

**Pay Range**
  
  
$23.26 - $31.62 Hourly
  
  
This position is under a step structure. Please note that the step placement is determined by your most recent completed academic year.

### **Additional Information**

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

**Why Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory?**

* Included in 2026 Best Places to Work by Glassdoor!
* Holiday Pay
* Sick leave accrual
* Individual 401(k) contributions
* Our values - visit https://www.llnl.gov/inclusion/our-values

**Security Clearance**

None required. However, if your assignment is longer than 179 days cumulatively within a calendar year, you must go through the Personal Identity Verification process. This process includes completing an online background investigation form and receiving approval of the background check.

**National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA)**

The 2025 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), Section 3112, generally prohibits citizens of China, Russia, Iran and North Korea without dual US citizenship or legal permanent residence from accessing specific non-public areas of national security or nuclear weapons facilities. The restrictions of NDAA Section 3112 apply to this position. To be qualified for this position, Candidates must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112.
